segments.text: All right, awesome conversation
happening right now, and I wanted to
chime in on it because people are
arguing whether if our best like
athletes play soccer, if we dominate the
sport. And this is obviously on the back
of that embarrassing loss to Belgium at
the World Cup. And there are some good
arguments, and I think there's some bad
ones as well. But for starters, America
is already closing the gap. There are
more Americans in the top five European
leagues than ever. Over the past decade,
the number of Americans in those leagues
and the minutes they play has more than
doubled, and each generation seems to
produce a star. Now, we can of course
rag on Pulisic after that performance,
but at 27, he's
already accomplished more stat-wise and
team-wise than any other American before
him. Again, the dude contributed to
winning the league. Now, where a lot of
non-Americans get it right is that
there's far more to the sport than just
physical gifts. They'll point to like
Messi, although I think he's stronger in
lower body than most people give him
credit for, but he's just not the most
physically opposing guy, and they
consider him the goat. And there's a
long list of the best footballers who
weren't great athletes, especially in
the midfield, like Kroos and and KDB.
Good luck slipping a piece of paper
under them when they jump. Yet, they're
still world-class. And if we are being
honest, that said, um there are guys
that are just phenomenal footballers
that had extraordinary gifts and were
extraordinary athletes, and they used
that ability. People pointing to Adama
Traoré isn't necessarily a good argument
cuz he's not world-class. That said,
Haaland is a freak athlete, and he is
world-class. In fact, that's what made
CR7 so dominant. Extremely technical,
but he was quick, he was fast, and he
could jump to the moon. And that's where
non-Americans should be a little more
considerate. Though I will concede a lot
of Americans are far too quick to this
argument, and they're making bad ones
out of arrogance, but think about where
those freak athletes come from, right?
You take a guy like Haaland, his pops
played ball, obviously. He was born in a
country and obviously his lineage is
from a country where football is the
number one sport. Guys that are 6'4, 6'5
in that build, they're not playing
soccer in our country, they're playing
basketball and football. I myself was a
solid athlete, I played soccer growing
up and I ran track all the way through
the collegiate level, but I only played
soccer by chance because I had a friend
that was into it. Guys like me naturally
gravitated towards other sports,
especially those that were far better
athletes than I ever was and I was a
again a decent one. I still have the
record over at Texas A&M University
Corpus Christi in the 100-meter dash. I
wasn't a slouch, but soccer isn't as
entrenched here.
Again, to further put this into
perspective, soccer is the number one
sport in the world. There are like only
35 countries where it isn't number one
and especially in the modern era, just
about all the great players, not just
good ones, the great ones, they come
from places where football is their
number one sport. So, it's not simply
about our best pro players in other
sports and what if they played soccer,
it's about all the athletes who never
went pro and got funneled elsewhere.
More young boys gravitate towards
football, basketball, and even baseball.
Soccer's it has grown, but until
recently there were like four other
sports that were more popular than it
here. So, it's not that soccer wasn't
the first option for our best athletes.
It wasn't the second, third, or the
fourth either and because those sports
are so contested, you've got great
athletes with great coordination who may
not have gone pro at all in the sport
that they wanted to be in and they never
ever even considered playing soccer. So,
two things can be true. Being physically
gifted isn't all there is to football,
But, there's also something to our best
athletes not playing the world sport.
Soccer is about touch, and technical
ability is something that if you're
going to operate at that level, you have
to be playing it since you're like 4
years old. If, and this is a big if, our
youth infrastructure was built around it
like the most, you know, European
countries, it'd look a lot different,
and it'll be interesting to see who's
coming up because the sport is getting
popular in America.
